source: Chapter 1.pdf, The Ever-Evolving World of Science, Curiosity Grade 7, reprint 2026-27
method: Inventory of the six visible source pages. The content model preserves these teaching points through documented rewriting. Duplicate hidden headings, production marks and running furniture are not teaching content. The Index supplies topic order.

points.point: Continue the Class 6 journey through questions, experiments and discovery in Class 7.
Science spans near and far, small and large: cells, celestial movements, household materials and groundwater.
Flight invites observation and curiosity.
points.treatment: Replace commentary about butterfly/plane folios with observing a real paper-plane flight. Omit unsupported aviation-history claims.

points.point: Science is a way of thinking, asking how and why, finding patterns and being open to the unknown.
Activities and experiments deepen understanding beyond reading a textbook.
Human activities, society and the natural world are connected; evidence helps address environmental challenges responsibly.
Physics, chemistry, biology and earth science are interconnected.
Explore material properties through questions about sour fruits and washing a haldi stain.
Batteries, lamps and wires connect circuits to material properties and grouping metals/non-metals.
Investigate changes and reversibility: a depleted battery, melting ice, ripening fruit and breaking rocks.
points.treatment: Correct the blanket depleted-battery claim: rechargeable and non-rechargeable types differ.

points.point: Heat moves and can cause changes; sunlight, evaporation, rainfall and groundwater connect.
points.treatment: Ice/glacier examples are consolidated as changes in water. Make condensation explicit; invisible vapour differs from cloud droplets.

points.point: Growing bodies change during the middle-school years.
points.treatment: Use the index term adolescence; add respectful discussion and variation between people.

points.point: Animals need food, breathing and circulation of nutrients; plants also need food and exchange gases.
Life processes developed as life evolved.
points.treatment: Remove the implication that organisms deliberately figured out or planned evolutionary changes.

points.point: Ask how time and speed are measured; changing shadows provide a connection with timekeeping.
points.treatment: Consolidate clock/watch and sundial examples into measuring time and tracking changing shadows.

points.point: Light enables seeing; light and shadow questions extend from familiar objects to the universe.
points.treatment: Lamps remain in the circuits tour; shadow-play illustration is replaced by the connection between shadows and timekeeping.

points.point: Earth rotates and orbits the Sun; the Moon orbits Earth. Connect these movements to day/night and shadows producing eclipses.
Experiments build on earlier knowledge; results that agree with expectations can still raise further questions.
Activity 1.1 Question the Answer: reverse the usual task and invent creative questions or situations.
The halving example can refer to equal cake shares, a long essay, fitting an envelope or a long dance song.
Preserve all four answers: crooked cat teeth; add milk; towel reassurance; 42.
Encourage interesting, non-obvious questions and continued exploration.
points.treatment: Remove textbook answer lines. Notebook responses include identifying assumptions. Creative premises are not established scientific explanations.

additions.reason: One focused first-hand investigation: matched paper planes, equal upturned tips on B, three alternating trials, first floor contact, controls and safe launching.
Interpret repeated observations without requiring a result; distinguish variation and evidence from a universal better-design claim.
Apply responsibility to school rainwater records and careful discussion without adding another investigation.
Six definitions, six retrieval points and four closing questions support the new reading sequence.

designDecisions: Keep 189 × 272 mm Science V2, Source Serif 4 body, Source Sans 3 headings and left alignment.
Use a scoped blue identity, regular serif numeral, semibold two-line title and matching vector paper-plane motifs.
The illustrated revision keeps the opener, seven lesson pages, combined reference page and final assessment in order. Extent follows readable pagination.
Retain one Investigate and two Think It Through panels. Whole panels, individual named topics with their picture/caption/bullets, and wide diagrams/captions are protected units.
The source topic tour is reordered using the supplied index. Chapters 2–12 remain references only.
